report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/council/vendors.py chunk 3: enforced policy claims in assemble/ask and CLI adapter plumbing; one broken claim (token ceiling) and several kept/uncheckable.
risks: ask line ~633 | high | Token ceiling enforced only when max_prompt_tokens is set; default None means unbounded spend despite docstring claiming per-call boundary. | Check default max_prompt_tokens in CouncilAdapter.__init__ or profile defaults; if None is default, ceiling is opt-in, not default.

assemble line ~589 | medium | WITHHELD notice lists blocked paths but does not state the lane name; readers may not know which egress rule applied. | Confirm lane is included elsewhere in the prompt (e.g., PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE) or intended to be implicit.

_interpret line ~683 | medium | Spawn error handling: any spawn_error not starting with 'not_on_path' is mapped to 'error'/'spawn_failed'; if spawn_error can be None, the branch is safe, but if it can be empty string, it would be misclassified. | Check RunResult.spawn_error type and whether empty string is possible.

ClaudeAdapter._parse_ok line ~734 | medium | Non-JSON output is treated as 'bad_response' error; if claude emits JSON with a different top-level shape (e.g., list), it also becomes 'bad_response'. That is strict but may be intended. | Confirm claude CLI contract always returns dict; if not, consider more specific handling.

_looks_unauthenticated line ~718 | low | Marker list is substring-based; a legitimate error containing 'invalid api key' as part of a longer phrase could be misclassified as auth failure. | Verify marker coverage and false-positive risk; consider regex boundaries.

handoff.purpose: Review CouncilAdapter.assemble/ask enforcement and CLI adapter subprocess plumbing.

symbols.name: CouncilAdapter.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes model, lane, repo_root, max_prompt_tokens, cli_version; validates lane against LANES.

symbols.name: CouncilAdapter.assemble
symbols.note: Builds outbound prompt; filters evidence paths/files by withheld; appends WITHHELD notice listing blocked paths.

symbols.name: CouncilAdapter.ask
symbols.note: Runs floor_check first; assembles prompt; enforces token ceiling if max_prompt_tokens set; dispatches via _dispatch; returns VendorReply.

symbols.name: CouncilAdapter._reply
symbols.note: Constructs VendorReply with vendor, actor, model, independence_class, endpoint, cli_version, lane, local, and kwargs.

symbols.name: _CliAdapter.__init__
symbols.note: Loads profile from COUNCIL_PROFILES, asserts safe, sets defaults, sets vendor and runner.

symbols.name: _CliAdapter.argv
symbols.note: Builds argv from profile command/args and optional model_arg.

symbols.name: _CliAdapter._dispatch
symbols.note: Spawns runner with stdin text, timeout, cwd via council_cwd, env via council_env.

symbols.name: _CliAdapter._interpret
symbols.note: Maps RunResult to status dict: spawn_error, timeout, auth failure, nonzero exit, else _parse_ok.

symbols.name: _CliAdapter._auth_failure
symbols.note: Default returns empty string; subclasses override.

symbols.name: _CliAdapter._parse_ok
symbols.note: Default returns status ok with stripped stdout as content and stderr tail.

symbols.name: _AUTH_MARKERS
symbols.note: Tuple of substring markers used by _looks_unauthenticated.

symbols.name: _looks_unauthenticated
symbols.note: Returns True if any marker appears in lowercase concatenation of blobs.

symbols.name: ClaudeAdapter
symbols.note: CLI adapter for Anthropic; overrides _auth_failure and _parse_ok.

symbols.name: ClaudeAdapter._auth_failure
symbols.note: Returns 'not_authenticated' if returncode not 0/None and _looks_unauthenticated on stderr/stdout.

symbols.name: ClaudeAdapter._parse_ok
symbols.note: Parses stdout as JSON; handles is_error, usage, total_cost_usd, duration_ms; returns ok or error.

symbols.name: CodexAdapter
symbols.note: CLI adapter for OpenAI; docstring claims always read-only sandbox.

claims.text: Withheld files are named but their contents are never rendered.
claims.why: Evidence files whose path is in blocked are skipped via `continue` before appending text; the WITHHELD notice only lists paths.

claims.text: The adapter -- not the caller -- renders the evidence blocks, because a gate that only REPORTS withheld paths while the caller ships the bytes anyway is worse than no gate.
claims.why: assemble is the only place evidence_files are rendered into the prompt; ask passes them to assemble and never sends them separately.

claims.text: FLOOR FIRST, on the raw caller inputs, before anything is assembled: the runner must not be reachable from a refused call.
claims.why: floor_check is called before assemble and before _dispatch; if refusal is not None, _dispatch is never reached.

claims.text: The runner is NOT invoked. The secret never leaves the process, and the recorded reason names the rule, never the bytes.
claims.why: On refusal, ask returns _reply directly with reason=refusal.rule and no content; no _dispatch call occurs.

claims.text: Charged BEFORE dispatch from the assembled prompt: a per-call timeout does not bound token spend, and reconciling after the call is not a budget.
claims.why: count_tokens is called on the assembled text before _dispatch; if over ceiling, returns error without dispatching.

claims.why: The code enforces token ceiling before dispatch; timeout_s only bounds the subprocess duration, not token count.

claims.why: The _dispatch call is wrapped in try/except Exception, converting any exception to a VendorReply error.

observations.what: Token ceiling is only enforced when max_prompt_tokens is not None; the docstring implies a per-call budget but the default may be None, making the ceiling opt-in.
The WITHHELD notice in assemble lists blocked paths but does not include the lane name; readers may not know which egress rule applied.
_interpret maps any spawn_error not starting with 'not_on_path' to 'error'/'spawn_failed'; if spawn_error can be empty string, it would be misclassified, but the code likely treats empty as no error.
ClaudeAdapter._parse_ok treats any non-dict JSON payload as 'bad_response'; if the CLI ever returns a list or other shape, it becomes an error rather than being parsed.
_looks_unauthenticated uses substring matching, which could produce false positives on legitimate error messages containing phrases like 'invalid api key'.
